questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Drive carefully.
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully.

questions.question: A passenger in a moving vehicle cannot:

options.text: Use a cell phone.
Sleep.
Have an open alcohol container.
Use a map.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have an open alcohol container.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to have an open alcohol container in a moving vehicle on a public road. The driver can be punished for this violation.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle share half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle with the same road rights as other vehicles. Give motorcyclists a complete lane. They need extra room to turn and stay safe.

questions.question: An arrow painted on the road means:

options.text: You may make the movement shown by the arrow if you choose.
You must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
You must always stop completely before making the movement shown by the arrow.
You must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the road tells you that you must make the movement it shows. Follow all traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before you turn or change lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before you turn or change lanes, look over your shoulder to see if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and get ready to stop.
Must stop and look for oncoming traffic before going.
May go through the intersection if it is safe.
Cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May go through the intersection if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can go through the intersection if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Drive slowly through the intersection.
Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You can turn in the direction the red arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop and stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Signs may show different rules.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
One-way traffic.
Limited parking.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Circular signs warn you of railroad crossings. This sign tells you a train crossing is near. Watch for oncoming trains.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes on an interstate. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies. Change lanes as few times as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: When should you use high beam headlights?

options.text: When driving in dark areas where you cannot see the road ahead.
In heavy fog.
When approaching the vehicle ahead of you.
When approaching oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving in dark areas where you cannot see the road ahead.
questions.explanation: High beam headlights help you see about 350 feet ahead. Use them in dark areas where you cannot see the road. Switch to low beams when you are within 500 feet of oncoming traffic or within 200 feet of the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to whom?

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout.
Bicyclists in the roundabout.
Pedestrians in the roundabout.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slowly release the accelerator and let your vehicle slow down. Once you are moving very slowly, apply the brakes gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of the vehicle.
On all sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to dangers. Do not crowd vehicles to your left and right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians pass before you go.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: You must yield to drivers on the public road when entering from a driveway or private road. Merge safely when it is clear.

questions.question: What happens if you refuse to take an alcohol test when suspected of drunk driving?

options.text: Your license will be suspended.
It is your right and there will be no consequences.
It is recommended.
You will only get a fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: When you drive a motor vehicle, you consent to an alcohol test. If you refuse the test, your driving privileges will be suspended.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be careful, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because few vehicles are coming.
By using the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Do not pass over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: What must other drivers allow for when driving near heavy trucks?

options.text: The longer stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
The shorter stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
The lower noise from larger vehicles.
The higher speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance needed by large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see the road ahead clearly.

questions.question: When can you drive across a dashed white line?

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross them to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down gently with the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently with the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Keep driving with the wheels off the pavement and slow down gently by applying the brakes. When you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not turn the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have larger blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that cannot be seen in the side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Flagger ahead.
Lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns of an upcoming intersection.
